Saudi wealth fund shelves medical distributor’s IPO
sum: Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund has dropped plans for an initial public offering of medical supplies distributor National Unified Procurement Company (NUPCO), more than two years after hiring banks for the deal, according to people familiar with the matter.

Public Investment Fund has in recent weeks told bankers to stop work on the IPO, which could have raised close to $1 billion, the people said, asking not to be identified. The decision is related to internal matters at NUPCO and not because of the impact of the regional war on investor appetite, the people said. It may decide to revive the share sale in the future, the people said.

Saudi Arabia had built depth in its domestic market over the past decade, opening up to foreigners and unleashing a wave of reforms to attract investors. That has given PIF and private business owners exit opportunities in a soaring stock market. But sentiment turned last year as state spending was cut and IPOs across the region have been frozen after the US-Iran war.

Three other Saudi companies decided not to proceed with share sales in August, Semafor previously reported. The Saudi index is down around 5% this year, a better performance than neighbors Bahrain, Kuwait, and Qatar, but lagging Abu Dhabi, Dubai, and Oman.
JPMorgan Chase & Co., Morgan Stanley, and SNB Capital were hired to work on the NUPCO IPO in 2024, Bloomberg previously reported.
- War is not the only culprit: Gulf firms are staying private for longer as part of a global phenomenon of weaker exit and IPO activity, a Pitchbook analyst told Semafor earlier this year.

sum: Most Gulf equities ended lower on Wednesday following the strikes on Saudi Arabia, as investors looked ahead to US inflation data that could influence the Federal Reserve rate decision.
Saudi Arabia's benchmark index dropped 0.6%, hit by a 1.2% fall in Al Rajhi Bank and a 0.9% decrease in the country's biggest lender by assets Saudi National Bank.

Elsewhere, oil major Saudi Aramco was down 0.2%. Yemen's Houthis on Wednesday claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, the kingdom's largest, which sits near a major crude export terminal. They also threatened to hit Jeddah and every other Saudi Red Sea port if Riyadh acts on its threats against Hodeidah. Both sides are now threatening strategic infrastructure. On Tuesday, a strike on Riyadh's tallest tower wounded at least 11 people, according to Saudi authorities, and the Saudi-led coalition vowed a firm response.

The kingdom on Tuesday approved a 2027 budget with planned spending of 1.39 trillion riyals ($370.44 billion) against projected revenue of 1.2 trillion riyals, leaving an estimated deficit of 190 billion riyals, state TV reported.

The US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) index, a key gauge closely watched by the central bank as it targets a 2% inflation rate, is due at 1330 GMT. Markets are fully pricing in a 25-basis-point rate increase at the Fed's policy meeting in December, according to CME's FedWatch tool. Monetary policy shifts in the US have a significant impact on Gulf markets, where most currencies are pegged to the dollar.
The Qatari benchmark fell 0.3%, with Qatar Islamic Bank losing 0.5%. Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index declined 0.7%, weighed down by a 2.3% slide in tobacco monopoly Eastern Co.

US Tech Stock Rebound Opens Opportunities for Saudi Companies, with HUMAIN in Spotlight
sum: Rapid developments in the US technology sector, led by Nvidia, have restored momentum to global stock markets following Jensen Huang's return as the company's chief executive. The move has revived confidence in artificial intelligence stocks and raised questions about how the new wave of investment could affect Gulf markets, particularly Saudi Arabia.

The announcement sparked a strong rally in Nvidia shares, with gains spreading across US equity markets as optimism over AI investment and digital infrastructure returned. The rebound has also brought renewed attention to companies and sectors linked to the AI ecosystem worldwide.

The recovery has extended to the Saudi stock market, where the benchmark Tadawul All Share Index (TASI) rose in early Tuesday trading as investors monitored global market developments and assessed how improving risk appetite could affect local equities.

Mohammed Al Farraj, Senior Director and Head of Asset Management at Arbah Capital, said the renewed momentum in US technology stocks should not be viewed merely as a temporary rebound in share prices, but as a clear indication of a revival in the global investment cycle associated with digital infrastructure.

Speaking to Asharq Al-Awsat, Al Farraj explained that the momentum would not necessarily translate into an automatic rise in Saudi Arabia's benchmark index, given the market's dependence on domestic drivers, including oil prices, government spending and corporate earnings.

He said the impact would be felt through three main channels: improved global liquidity and risk appetite, increased capital expenditure on infrastructure, and a revaluation of local companies connected to the AI ecosystem.

Discussing the Saudi sectors most likely to benefit from renewed global investment in artificial intelligence, Al Farraj said opportunities span interconnected industries that together form an integrated value chain.

The Anthropic IPO Raised $81 Billion. The Stock Market Fell Anyway.
sum: Anthropic stock (ANT) priced at $83 and jumped 17% on its debut — but a $1.5 trillion valuation, 90 pages of risk factors, and a falling Nasdaq tell a more complicated story

On Wednesday night, Anthropic — the five-year-old company behind the Claude chatbot — priced its shares at $83, well above the $70 to $78 range it had pitched to investors. Demand was so heavy the deal grew: 980 million shares, about $81.3 billion raised, plus another $26 billion in private financing on top. That makes it the largest IPO in history, ahead of SpaceX's $75 billion debut earlier this year and, way back in third place, Saudi Aramco's $29.4 billion in 2019.

At $83 a share, the company walked onto the Nasdaq on Thursday valued at roughly $1.5 trillion, counting everything on a fully diluted basis. The stock opened at $111.50, which is the kind of number that makes anchors use the word "pop." It closed around $97, up 17%.
The Dow dropped 1,101 points. The S&P 500 lost 2%. The Nasdaq sank 2.25%, its sixth straight rough session in a sell-off that a record-breaking debut was meant to interrupt and didn't.
That split screen — one company minting thousands of new millionaires while the index it just joined keeps sliding — is the whole AI story in 2026, in one trading day.
Part of the price is scarcity, and scarcity is doing a lot of quiet work here.

Anthropic is the first major frontier AI lab to go public. If you run a large fund and your benchmark is filling up with AI exposure, there has simply not been a pure way to buy "the Claude company" until now. Reports from the pricing put demand at nearly seven times the shares on offer. Index funds will have to buy more in the coming weeks as ANT gets added to benchmarks — one estimate put forced buying at around $19 billion in the first month alone.

Private Credit’s $100 Billion Saudi Prize Is Proving Hard to Win
sum: (Bloomberg) -- Many private credit firms believe Saudi Arabia offers an estimated $100 billion opportunity, potentially helping transform the Middle East into one of the biggest markets for the asset class. But deploying capital at the required scale and speed is proving difficult.

A recent $150 million financing for a little-known Saudi firm illustrates the challenge. Backed by Goldman Sachs Group Inc., HSBC Holdings Plc, Fortress Investment Group and at least three regional fund managers, and small by Wall Street standards, the deal took months to complete.

Delays over regulation, deal structure and the investor mix complicated a transaction that would have taken just weeks to put together in many other markets, according to people familiar with the matter, who asked not to be identified discussing private information.
That disconnect is awkward for the largest Gulf economy, which is in the midst of a multitrillion-dollar overhaul.

Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman’s plans to diversify away from oil require vast private investment across sectors including artificial intelligence. Just as borrowing needs rise, near-daily attacks by the Houthis are adding to the pressure, weighing on economic activity, exacerbating a liquidity crunch and denting investor confidence.

“The conflict has fundamentally reinforced the strategic importance of private capital for Saudi Arabia,” said Atefeh Ebadian, chief economist and investment strategist at Dubai-based Symax Group, whose work focuses on Gulf economies and evaluating private investment opportunities. “It has also changed the urgency.”

Yet, regulatory uncertainty, licensing timelines and rules around local presence are impeding progress and slowing the flow of capital, according to more than a dozen fund managers. Even firms that clear those hurdles face difficulty deploying money, they said, pointing to a pipeline dominated by small companies and returns that may not always adequately compensate for the extra effort and risk.

Anthropic’s record IPO: Wall Street bets on AI as company warns of “existential” risks
sum: Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI models, began trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday after raising $81.3 billion in the largest initial public offering in history. The stock opened at $111.50, 34 percent above its offering price, briefly valuing the company at roughly $2 trillion on a fully diluted basis, before closing at $97.17.

The offering surpassed by $6.3 billion the previous record of $75 billion, set by Elon Musk’s SpaceX in June, which had itself more than doubled the roughly $29 billion raised by Saudi Aramco in 2019. Amid what sources told CNBC was the largest retail demand for any IPO, Anthropic upsized the sale to 980 million shares and priced them above its marketed range. On Friday, the company announced that its underwriters had exercised their option to buy an additional 147 million shares, raising the total to about $93.5 billion, more than SpaceX ultimately raised after its own underwriters did the same.

The offering delivered a windfall to Wall Street. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley led a syndicate of banks, including JPMorgan, Citigroup and Barclays, that will divide underwriting fees estimated in the hundreds of millions of dollars. The company’s seven founders now have net worths exceeding $20 billion, while over 3,000 employees are now multimillionaires on paper.

Far more than a financial transaction, the offering is a political and geopolitical event. It came at the conclusion of a political operation that removed Nvidia’s Jensen Huang, the leading corporate opponent of decoupling the US and Chinese economies. The flotation of Anthropic, the industry’s most outspoken advocate of cutting China off from advanced chips, is a declaration by the American financial oligarchy that it is staking colossal sums, and the global position of US imperialism, on dominance in AI, regardless of the consequences.

The speculation is all the more striking given the market into which the shares were sold. On November 5, the Nasdaq fell 5.52 percent, erasing some $3.2 trillion in technology market value and setting off a global selloff. Nvidia, whose chips power the boom, has lost about $2.5 trillion in market value since its October 6 peak.

Broadcom passes Saudi Aramco to become the world’s eighth most valuable company
sum: The chipmaker's market value reached about $1.75 trillion, edging past the Saudi oil giant in a ranking that keeps changing hands
Broadcom has moved past Saudi Aramco to become the world’s eighth most valuable company, with a market value of about $1.75 trillion.
Broadcom (AVGO) reached a peak valuation of roughly $1.75 trillion. That was enough to temporarily overtake Aramco (2222.SR) for eighth place on the global market cap leaderboard.
Aramco sat close behind. The Saudi company was valued at roughly $1.70 to $1.702 trillion around mid-November 2026.
The ranking was tight enough to flip in both directions. Research tied to the move shows that as of the November 13 and 17, 2026 market closes, the order was reversed.
On those dates, Aramco held about $1.70 to $1.702 trillion and the eighth spot. Broadcom sat in ninth at around $1.656 to $1.69 trillion.

For context, the companies at the very top operate on a different scale. The November 2026 leaderboard was led by Apple at about $5.18 trillion, Nvidia at about $3.93 trillion, and Microsoft at about $3.89 trillion.

5 Oil and Gas Stocks That Crushed Third-Quarter Earnings Estimates
sum: We are currently at the tail-end of the third quarter earnings season, with more than 90% of S&P 500 companies having reported, and it's proven to be yet another bumper season. According to FactSet data, the index has reported 31.9% Y/Y average earnings growth, marking the third consecutive quarter that earnings growth has exceeded 25%. All 11 sectors of the U.S. market have posted positive earnings and revenue growth, with seven reporting double-digit earnings growth led by the energy, IT and materials sectors.
The energy sector has posted the highest earnings growth amongst the 11 sectors at 151.2% Y/Y as well as the second-highest revenue growth at 35.7% Y/Y, thanks to higher energy prices.

Oil prices averaged $85.68/bbl in the third quarter, ~32% higher compared to the corresponding quarter a year ago. At the sub-industry level, 4 of the 5 sub-industries in the energy sector have reported positive earnings growth led by Oil & Gas Refining & Marketing (542%), Integrated Oil & Gas (141%), Oil & Gas Exploration & Production (83%), and Oil & Gas Storage & Transportation (30%). Only the Oil & Gas Equipment & Services (-3%) sub-industry has reported a decline in earnings.
Here are 5 Oil & Gas Companies that have easily exceeded Wall Street expectations:

Record Permian Basin volumes lifted ONEOK's (NYSE:OKE) third-quarter earnings, and the Tulsa-based pipeline operator is raising its spending to add processing, pipeline and export capacity in the Permian and on the Gulf Coast. ONEOK gathers, processes, transports and stores natural gas, natural gas liquids (NGLs), refined products and crude oil across a 60,000-mile network linking producers to domestic and international markets. NGL raw feed throughput rose 6% to nearly 1.7 million barrels per day, with the Gulf Coast/Permian region up 16%. Refined products shipments climbed 6% and Permian gas processing volumes rose 4%. Those gains raised adjusted EBITDA 6% year-over-year to $2.24 billion.

ONEOK's headline earnings of $2.13 per diluted share beat the consensus by 63 cents, though 53 cents of that came from a one-time, non-cash tax benefit tied to a corporate reorganization. Stripped of the benefit, the company still beat consensus by a dime.

Rahul Gandhi counters BJP over ‘Mumma on Papa’s lap’ row, shares Lord Shiva-Goddess Parvati photo message
sum: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi expressed that fear, anger, and hatred obstruct love among BJP and RSS supporters. He believes it is his duty as a Hindu to help them overcome these negative emotions. Gandhi's remarks coincided with the launch of his mother Sonia Gandhi's memoir, which stirred political controversy. Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma criticized Gandhi for his comments about divinity.
“Fear, anger and hatred have woven a web in the hearts of BJP and RSS supporters that stops them from experiencing and expressing love,” he tweeted.

He added, “As a true Hindu, it is my duty to free them from this web, so that they too can start to experience the breathtaking beauty and joy of love and belonging in their lives. Satyam Shivam Sundaram.”
Gandhi shared the post along with an image of a 12th-century Hoysala sculpture showing Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati seated atop Nandi, the bull, at the Hoysaleshwara Temple in Halebidu, Karnataka.
“A person's decline accelerates the moment they stop standing before God and start posing as one,” he tweeted.

The exchange comes a day after Gandhi's comments about his parents' relationship at the launch of his mother Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, sparked a political controversy, with Sarma among the leading critics.
Speaking about his childhood, Gandhi recalled the affection between his parents and said his mother would often sit on his father's lap during family meals.

Ben explained that he lives in KAFD, just a short distance from the Aramco building that sustained limited damage following the incident.
He described the district as much more than a collection of impressive skyscrapers, calling it a place where people live, work and build their futures.
For Ben, KAFD represents Saudi Arabia’s incredible transformation, bringing together futuristic architecture, talented people and ambitious opportunities

sum: The Houthis, who control most of the populous parts of Yemen, have intensified attacks on the Saudi capital in recent days

The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis said on Sunday it had intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles launched towards the Saudi capital Riyadh and three drones in the kingdom's oil-rich Eastern Province.
The Eastern Province, the economic powerhouse of Saudi Arabia, has been subject to multiple attacks by Houthis in the past few weeks.
It contains the majority of the kingdom's oil and gas reserves and is home to Aramco's headquarters, which suffered extensive damage in an attack in October.
The Houthis have stepped up strikes on Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities, while Saudi Arabia has ramped up airstrikes on Houthi targets in Yemen in response.

Houthis claim missile strike on Saudi Forces in Jazan
sum: Sanaa, Nov 14: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi group on Friday claimed to have fired two ballistic missiles at what it described as concentrations of Saudi forces in Al-Tuwal, in the Jazan province of Saudi Arabia.
The claim came hours after Saudi civil defence authorities issued an all-clear for the province. It was not immediately clear whether the reported missile attack was connected to the earlier alerts.

Jazan is home to a Saudi Aramco refinery with a capacity to process 400,000 barrels of crude oil per day. Southern Saudi Arabia, which shares a border with Yemen, has repeatedly faced Houthi missile and drone attacks targeting military installations and energy infrastructure, including the Jazan refinery.

In a separate statement, the Houthis also claimed to have targeted King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and a pumping station along Saudi Arabia's East-West Pipeline. Saudi authorities had not immediately confirmed the claims.

Amid disruptions to oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz due to the ongoing Middle East conflict, Saudi Arabia has diverted around four million barrels of crude oil per day through the East-West Pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. This accounts for approximately four per cent of global oil supply.

Meanwhile, fighting between the Houthis and the coalition supporting Yemen's internationally recognised government has intensified. The escalation follows the Houthi advance in September towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a strategic shipping route at the southern entrance to the Red Sea.

sum: Africa’s biggest money manager and Nigerian pension-fund administrators applied for almost $1 billion of shares in Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE, according to people familiar with the matter.

The Public Investment Corp, which oversees almost $220 billion in assets, including pensions for South African state workers, asked for about $500 million of shares in the initial public offering, said the people who asked not to be identified as the information is still private.
Dangote refinery seeks to raise between $1.6 billion and $2.1 billion in the continent’s biggest IPO to date.
Aliko Dangote, Africa’s richest man, could consider selling down some of his own stake in his Lagos refinery to meet the request in a secondary sale, said the people.

Nigerian pension administrators operating in the nation’s Contributory Pension Scheme system — which has about 11 million members spread across 20 funds — have applied for about $400 million to $500 million of shares in the continent’s top oil refinery, part of which was covered by an earlier private placement, said the people, declining to identify the funds.

Dangote didn’t respond to a request for comment. The PIC declined to comment. A spokesperson for the Pension Fund Operators Association of Nigeria, the umbrella body for the retirement-fund industry, didn’t respond to a request for comment.

items.t: DRTECH's bendable detector approved for use by Saudi Aramco and ADNOC
sum: DRTECH said Thursday that it has received final end-user approval from Saudi Aramco and the United Arab Emirates' Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) for its bendable X-ray detectors, which convert X-ray images into digital data.
The company plans to accelerate its push into the global industrial nondestructive testing (NDT) market.
DRTECH said the approvals from the two state-owned oil companies validate the performance of its proprietary bendable detectors for industrial applications.

Until now, film-based analog methods have dominated inspections of pipeline welds. The company expects the approvals to accelerate the adoption of digital NDT solutions, which offer greater inspection efficiency.

DRTECH has been expanding its bendable detector lineup through active research and development. It has developed 4-inch, 8-inch and 16-inch models and recently introduced a compact 2-inch model for inspecting small-diameter pipelines. The expanded lineup allows the company to serve a wide range of pipeline sizes, from small to large diameters.

The company is also expanding supplies of its bendable detectors in North America. Earlier this year, it supplied a 16-inch model for inspecting large-diameter pipelines to Company A, the region's largest specialized NDT provider. It recently secured additional approval to supply a new model capable of inspecting small-diameter pipelines as narrow as 2 inches.

Company A has annual revenue of 1.6 trillion won and provides NDT and facility management services across various industries, including oil and gas, shipbuilding, chemicals and aerospace, primarily in the United States and Canada.

Intuitive Machines Surges 16% on Record Quarter and Positive Free Cash Flow; AST SpaceMobile Falls 3%, Rocket Lab Slips 2%
sum: This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.

A record quarter is pulling Intuitive Machines (NASDAQ:LUNR) away from the rest of the space group amid a broad pullback in growth stocks. Intuitive Machines stock is at $14.19, up 16% in early morning trading. The company released its Q3 2026 results before the open on November 12 and beat expectations on both revenue and loss per share.

Third-quarter revenue at Intuitive Machines reached $269.35 million, exceeding the $247.56 million consensus estimate and rising 413.7% from a year earlier. Satellite production from the January Lanteris acquisition drove most of that growth, adding $215.12 million of revenue. CEO Steve Altemus declared, “In the third quarter, we delivered record financial performance across the board.”

Cash generation sets this report apart. Intuitive Machines produced operating cash flow of $66 million and free cash flow of $33 million, a record. Backlog at the company climbed to a record $1.87 billion from $213 million at December 31, 2025.

NASA also named Intuitive Machines a vendor on its $10 billion Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) 2 contract. Looking ahead, Intuitive Machines expects full-year 2026 revenue of $920 million to $950 million along with positive adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization.

Skeptics have reasons for caution about Intuitive Machines. A $30.01 million gain from the change in fair value of warrant liabilities helped the company post a loss of $0.02 per share, narrower than the $0.11 loss analysts expected. Acquisition costs and a non-recurring legal expense partly offset that gain, yet the company’s $34.2 million operating loss shows the core business still isn’t profitable.
One-time program adjustments also raised gross margin at Intuitive Machines. Free cash flow at the company stands at negative $112.3 million year to date, even after the strong quarter.

Tankers continue to burn in the Middle East despite hopes for de-escalation, Asia News
sum: Despite market bets on a de-escalation in the Iran war, new evidence has emerged in recent days of strikes on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and on energy infrastructure in the Middle East.

On Tuesday (Nov 10), crude prices hit two-month lows after US officials downplayed the need for additional military action against Iran, with analysts noting President Donald Trump's more conciliatory tone since the Republicans' defeat in the Nov 3 midterm elections.

However, there is little sign of attacks abating in November, after 37 ships were attacked in October, the highest monthly total since the start of the war, according to data from the Washington Institute for Near East Policy.

Videos posted on social media on Sunday and verified by Reuters showed a Navig8 tanker on fire near the coast of Oman. An image captured by the European Union's Copernicus Sentinel-2 satellite on Sunday showed a large cloud of black smoke at the same location.
It was one of three tankers hit on Sunday for using "unauthorised routes" through the strait, Iranian state broadcaster IRIB reported, citing the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy.
The vessel is managed by Navig8, majority owned by ADNOC Logistics & Services. Neither replied to emailed Reuters requests for comment.

At the same time, US forces continued to enforce a naval blockade of Iranian ports. In the latest incident, a US military aircraft fired on and disabled a St Kitts-flagged cargo vessel that tried to depart regional waters after visiting an Iranian port on Saturday, US Central Command said.

Saudi-led coalition reports Houthi missile, drone interceptions; Saba reports Saudi strikes on Sanaa
sum: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen said on Tuesday (Nov 10) it intercepted two missiles launched by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis towards Riyadh, a ballistic missile fired towards the kingdom's southern region and a drone over its oil-rich Eastern Province, in a night of heightened military activity across Saudi Arabia.

The latest launches come amid an escalation in hostilities between the Houthis and the coalition backing Yemen's internationally recognised government after the group advanced in September towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, a strategic shipping chokepoint at the southern entrance to the Red Sea.
The Houthis have since stepped up strikes on Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities, while Saudi Arabia has carried out airstrikes on Houthi targets in Yemen.

The coalition said its air defences had destroyed a ballistic missile and a cruise missile fired towards the Saudi capital. Saudi Civil Defence had earlier issued an early-warning alert for Riyadh before later saying the threat had passed.
In a separate statement, the coalition said it had intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched towards southern Saudi Arabia, which borders Yemen.
Saudi Civil Defence had previously issued warning alerts for the southwestern cities of Abha and Khamis Mushait, before later saying the danger had passed.

The Houthi-run Saba news agency reported that Saudi Arabia carried out airstrikes on Yemen's Houthi-controlled capital Sanaa, hitting the al-Mufazir gas station in the Jadar district north of the capital and a building belonging to the state oil company in southern Sanaa.

Saudi civil defence sounds all-clear after alerts in southern cities, Asia News
sum: Saudi Arabia's civil defence on Sunday (Nov 8) lifted alerts in several areas of the kingdom's oil-rich Eastern Province, including Dhahran, home to the headquarters of oil major Saudi Aramco, shortly after warning of potential danger.
The all-clear also applies to Dammam, Abqaiq and Al-Ahsa governorate, the civil defence said.
The Eastern Province contains the majority of the kingdom's oil and gas reserves as well as Saudi Aramco's headquarters, which suffered extensive damage in an attack in October.
Shortly after the all-clear, the Saudi-led coalition fighting in Yemen said it had intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Yemeni Iran-allied Houthi group towards the Eastern region.

The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at Saudi airports, ports and oil installations, turning US ally Saudi Arabia into a pressure point in a war that began with the US and Israel attacking Iran in February.

Oil Rebounds Toward $100 as Democrats' Sweep Rattles Energy Stocks
sum: Oil prices reversed their recent downtrend on Thursday, a day after Democrats swept control of both the House and Senate, creating a potential legislative check on U.S. President Donald Trump’s administration. Brent crude was up 4.0% to trade at $98.38 per barrel at 3:15 pm ET, while WTI gained 2.9% to $90.65, with prices rising for the first time in four sessions after plunging to a near two-month low on Wednesday. U.S. natural gas prices were flat at $2.95/MMBtu, while European gas prices rebounded 1.9% to €89.72/MWh. The U.S. stock market resumed its recent downtrend on Thursday, with the S&P 500 down more than 3% and the Nasdaq off about 5% in afternoon trading as a selloff in AI chip stocks deepened. AI stocks tied to Texas data centers were hit hard after Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated long-serving Texas governor Greg Abbott, with CoreWeave (NASDAQ:CRWV) falling 7% and Nebius Group (NASDAQ:NBIS) and Oracle (NYSE:ORCL) each sliding 4% in overnight trading on Wednesday. Hinojosa has called for a pause on new data-center projects until protections for electricity supplies, water resources and local communities are in place, with investors fearing similar roadblocks could slow down the AI data center boom once Democratic governors take office in January 2027.

The energy investment universe was a mixed bag, with the oil and gas benchmark, State Street Energy Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLE), falling 1.6% to $62.50 on Thursday, as energy stocks tracked the broader market lower despite the rebound in crude. Wednesday’s 8.7% plunge in Brent priced in bets that the election setback would force the Trump administration to pursue a peace deal with Iran and reopen Hormuz.

Those bets faded on Thursday, with Eurasia Group cutting its odds of a negotiated agreement to 10% from 20% and putting the likelihood of renewed U.S. strikes at 60%, while Iran’s navy reported that a tanker struck a mine east of the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire. President Trump acknowledged the war’s role in the Republican losses but said the conflict has been worth it.
Additionally, Democratic committee chairs are set to deploy their new subpoena powers from January to investigate the administration’s energy dealings.

items.t: 3 Private Deals Executed on the Saudi Stock Exchange, Valued at SAR 49 Million
sum: On Monday, November 2, 2026, three private deals were executed on the Saudi Stock Exchange ("Tadawul"), involving 2.2 million shares of Saudi Aramco, Saudi Electrical Industries, and AlAhli Bank. The total value of these transactions reached approximately SAR 49 million.

A private transaction occurs when both the seller and the buyer agree upon the quantity and price of the listed securities involved. Regarding settlement, these negotiated transactions can be settled within a timeframe ranging from T+0 to T+5, as agreed upon by the parties; if no specific settlement period is determined by the seller and buyer, a T+2 settlement cycle is applied automatically.

Furthermore, transactions executed during any additional trading sessions must comply with daily price fluctuation limits and minimum transaction value requirements. Negotiated transactions may be carried out during the following sessions: the pre-opening auction, the open market session, the closing auction, the market-closed session, and the post-closing session.

The pre-opening auction and post-closing sessions are made available once the lead underwriter or the transaction coordinator submits a formal request and fulfills all requirements set by the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul) for enabling these sessions.

Google, Nvidia Led $3.17T AI Stock Slide; Only Four Rose
sum: Thirty large AI-exposed stocks lost a combined $3.17 trillion of market value in October, from $37.53 trillion at the end of September to $34.36 trillion at the close on 30 October, an 8.5% fall by our arithmetic. Only four of the 30 rose.

Alphabet, Google’s parent, and Nvidia together lost $1.35 trillion, 43% of the total. The gainers were Tesla, Apple, Microsoft and IBM, and the month ended on the day Apple passed Nvidia as the most valuable company.
A short Business Engineer explainer on power laws, where a few outcomes account for most of the value. It teaches the general idea only and does not discuss the companies in this story.

By our arithmetic, Alphabet lost $780.2 billion (18.5%), Nvidia $572.1 billion (10.4%), Intel $289.5 billion (45.3%), Meta $281.7 billion (15.2%) and Micron $204.1 billion (16.9%). Those five account for $2.13 trillion, or 67% of the group’s fall.

Memory makers fell together: Micron, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics lost a combined $549.5 billion. Chip-equipment makers Applied Materials, Lam Research, KLA and ASML lost $350.9 billion between them.

The steepest percentage falls were Intel at 45.3%, CoreWeave at 37.0%, Arm at 28.9% and Lam Research at 27.2%. Intel’s shares fell 28.6% on 30 October alone after its results, as we reported on Friday.
Tesla added $177.9 billion (12.7%), Apple $169.4 billion (3.5%), Microsoft $66.9 billion (1.8%) and IBM $35.8 billion (17.2%), by our arithmetic. Salesforce was close to flat, down $0.3 billion.

Having world's most reliable alternatives propel Aramco shares to their highest level in over a year
sum: Saudi Aramco shares rose 4.1% at the close of trading on Sunday, March 8, 2026, settling at SAR 26.94 per share, marking their highest closing price in over a year, specifically since March 3, 2025. This strong surge is supported by a jump in global oil prices (Brent crude surpassed $92) and escalating geopolitical tensions, boosting the performance of energy sector stocks and fueling expectations of strong earnings.
Aramco holds a leading position as one of the world's largest energy and chemicals companies, contributing to global trade and improving the daily lives of millions of people worldwide.

Despite geopolitical challenges, Saudi Aramco possesses strategic alternatives for exporting oil to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, most notably the Petroline (East-West) pipeline, which transports crude oil to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea. This expansion enables the export of approximately 5-7 million barrels per day westward, in addition to relying on strategic Asian reserves to ensure continued supply.

Saudi Aramco is the world’s most reliable energy supplier, with a proven track record of delivering no shipments to its customers for operational reasons in over 90 years. It is committed to a 99.9% supply reliability rate, maintaining its position as the world’s largest integrated energy company and demonstrating its ability to respond quickly to supply challenges, as evidenced by its handling of past operational crises.
Its historical record includes: no shipments delayed for operational reasons in 90 years, and a 99.9% supply reliability rate across its refining, chemicals, and marketing sector.
